sources.title: Korea Tourism Organization photograph: numbered pit garages
sources.observation: Actual numbered shutters 25–28, pale concrete apron, blue strip and yellow lane edge. The listing reports 32 pits; individual apron box outlines are not visible.
sources.publisher: Korea Tourism Organization; listing served by KTourMap
sources.captureDateStatus: Unknown; other images in the same set show a 2023 track-festival banner.

sources.title: Korea Tourism Organization photograph: main straight and pit building
sources.observation: Long two-storey silver/white pit building is on the infield side of the straight, opposite the roofed grandstand; low concrete pit wall separates its apron.

sources.title: Korea Tourism Organization photograph: four-storey control tower
sources.observation: Four visible storeys at the downstream end of the pit building; flat roof, pale cladding and continuous greenish glazing.

sources.title: Taebaek Speedway official course map
sources.observation: Operator plan identifies start, paddock and grandstand. It is schematic and establishes the infield side and ordering, not surveyed building corners.

metadata.coverage: Race pit building, control tower, working apron, pit lane and wall; photo-based approximate footprint.

registration.method: Track-relative placement on main straight, infield/driver-right side; operator start/paddock diagram and opposite-grandstand photographs.

limitations: No measured building plan or orthophoto obtained; footprint/entry positions are approximate.
The 32 garage total is from the tourism listing; exact current allocation and apron box paint were not verified.
No individual painted pit-stop boxes invented; garage modules and open working apron are shown.
Tourism photographs are retained locally for review only; capture date unknown, a companion photo displays 2023.

properties.evidence: Long garage row observed opposite the grandstand. 32 total garages follows the tourism listing, with numbered bays 25–28 independently visible in the close photograph.
